clue.text: Upright, so may share our secret

definitions.text: Upright, so may share our secret

parts.words: Upright, so may share our secret
parts.note: a vertical part of a bed, invoked in the saying 'between you, me and the ...' when a confidence is shared

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'between you and me and the bedpost' marks a secret; the upright post of the bed is the third party privy to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's corner upright is the post named in the old idiom for keeping a confidence.

clue.text: Sportingly, he takes over

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls, faced by the player at the crease

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes over' looks like assuming control; in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, which the man at the crease receives.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer at the crease receives the six-ball overs bowled at him.

clue.text: In such rain, it's better than walking

definitions.text: In such rain, it's better than walking

parts.words: In such rain, it's better than walking
parts.note: the adjective for heavy wind-blown rain is also the activity of going by car

explanation.walkthrough: Wind-lashed rain is described this way, and in such weather going by car beats going on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy wind-blown rain is called this, and so is travelling by car.

clue.text: Not being in the same thing makes one excel

parts.note: out means not in
do is short for ditto, the same thing again

explanation.surface: Being different is what makes a person stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the short form of ditto, used in lists for 'the same again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass a rival is to excel beyond them.

clue.text: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work

definitions.text: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work

parts.words: Circulatory system forcing one to walk to work
parts.note: circulatory suggests the blood, but this is a turning belt on which a person walks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulatory system' points to heart and blood; it is a belt going round, once a prison punishment, now a gym machine and a byword for drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A looping exercise belt, and figuratively monotonous routine labour.

clue.text: Told of a family connection?

definitions.meaning: narrated, as a story is recounted
kin to someone, connected by blood or marriage

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they were informed about a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a tale is to recount it, and people who are kin are relations of each other.

clue.text: Come round again about a despicable chap

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A rotter turns up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens repeatedly comes back time after time.

clue.text: They are utterly conclusive

parts.note: utterly means by way of utterance, so these are the final things spoken

explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' seems to mean completely; here it means in what is uttered.
explanation.definitionFit: The final remarks spoken by someone, especially before death.

clue.text: Defeat in counter-revolution

indicators.note: the letters of counter are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellion is crushed by a counter-revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent heavily is to defeat them.

clue.text: Glance shows a student in fault

indicators.note: the learner is placed within the word for fault

parts.note: a defect is a fault
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A look reveals a pupil's error.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that glances off a surface is turned aside from its path.

clue.text: A plant from the list

indicators.note: the letters are made from the words that follow, so they are rearranged to form a new word

explanation.surface: Someone picks a flower off a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a thin anagram signal here: the seven letters of THE LIST are reworked into the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly wild flower, Scotland's emblem, is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Prepare to sail away after the players

indicators.note: the word for away is placed after the word for the players

parts.note: the actors in a production are its cast
off, as in gone away

explanation.surface: A crew readies a boat to leave once the performers are aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Untying a vessel's mooring lines before departure is the nautical sense of the phrase.

clue.text: How a knight obtains his armour?

definitions.text: How a knight obtains his armour?

parts.words: How a knight obtains his armour?
parts.note: chain armour is called mail, and he might send off for it rather than buy it in a shop

explanation.walkthrough: MAIL is linked metal armour; the phrase normally means buying goods by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying by post is a shopping method, and mail is also chain armour a knight would wear.

clue.text: Start with pain

parts.note: start here means a sudden flinch or jerk, made because something hurts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' seems to mean begin, but it is the involuntary jump of someone hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A flinch or grimace caused by sudden hurt is a jerk of the body made in response to suffering.

clue.text: Leading Abyssinian drink

definitions.meaning: the title of Ethiopia's ruler, Abyssinia being the old name of Ethiopia
a hot mixture of port or sherry with sugar, lemon and spice

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian notable takes a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ethiopian emperor's title is shared with a warm spiced wine punch.

clue.text: One who helps to shed the load

definitions.text: One who helps to shed the load

parts.words: One who helps to shed the load
parts.note: shed suggests casting off a burden, but the load is a ship's cargo being taken off at the docks

explanation.walkthrough: 'shed the load' sounds like relief from worry; it is unloading cargo from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dock labourer unloads cargo from vessels.

clue.text: A grave commitment

parts.note: grave suggests serious, but here it is the burial plot to which a body is committed

explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' wants to be the adjective 'serious'; it is the noun, a place of burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing a body to the earth is burial.

clue.text: The big swell may be a bore

definitions.meaning: a surge of water up a river on the tide, as on the River Severn

explanation.surface: A grand toff might turn out to be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big swell' and 'bore' look like a posh person and a dull one; both are surges of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea surge, and also a tidal surge up an estuary.

clue.text: Dissipated period died out

indicators.note: the word died is spread out so another word can sit in its middle

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dissolute stretch of life came to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' splits DIED as DI...ED around SPELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts or fog that have been scattered or driven away have been dissipated.

clue.text: Doctor should prescribe no water

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: A physician tells a patient to avoid fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prescribe' links the pieces in the surface but gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rain leaves the land dry.

clue.text: Cast in a devilish mould

indicators.note: the letters are poured into a fresh mould and come out reshaped

explanation.surface: Something is formed in a fiendish shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mould' reshapes CAST IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the Devil, fiendish.

clue.text: Country school you realise is achieving, initially

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five words before it are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A pupil is told their school is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: Sumptuously entertains a chap with drinks

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A host lavishly treats a fellow to beers.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast or delight guests lavishly.

clue.text: Criticises a levy, we hear

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a tax is a levy

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a new charge, it is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone verbally is to assail them in words.

clue.text: How fantastic to be out and about

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: How wonderful to be out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bizarre or eccentric is fantastic in the sense of strange.

clue.text: Combat in which one is put to the sword

definitions.text: Combat in which one is put to the sword

parts.words: Combat in which one is put to the sword
parts.note: a spectacle in which a matador kills the animal with a blade

explanation.walkthrough: 'one' sounds like a person slain in battle; it is the animal in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador's contest ends with a blade thrust into the animal.

clue.text: Nerve — but not of steel

definitions.meaning: a yellow alloy of copper and zinc, a metal other than steel

explanation.surface: Someone has a cheek, but no nerves of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'nerves of steel'; the answer is cheek, and a metal that is not steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is called cheek in British slang, and it is also a copper-zinc alloy.

clue.text: Give up in pro game

parts.note: for means in favour of, pro
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A player concedes during a professional match.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or do without something is to relinquish it.

clue.text: Canal-boat almost departed with wrong load

indicators.note: the word for departed loses its last letter, falling just short

parts.note: gone means departed

indicators.note: the letters of load are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A Venetian boat left carrying a badly stowed cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GONE to GON; 'wrong' turns LOAD into DOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat-bottomed boats of Venice ply its canals.

clue.text: Bill and Cyril worked producing fibre

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: the name Cyril is worked into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Cyril made a textile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' turns CYRIL into RYLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic textile yarn made from a polymer.

clue.text: They admit they're often punched

parts.note: admit means let in, and the punching is a conductor clipping holes, not violence

explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' looks like confessing, and 'punched' like assault; these are passes of entry clipped by an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes for travel or entry are clipped by an inspector and grant entry.

clue.text: "I" gets so replicated by them

indicators.note: copied out in a fresh form, so these letters appear in another order

explanation.surface: Self-centred people say 'I' over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replicated' reworks I, GETS and SO; the whole clue also describes self-obsessed people repeating 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred people constantly put themselves first in speech.
